title: The Offer
body:
> ✅ **FINALIZED 2026-07-11 — 3-tier ladder.** Names + roles locked: **Premium** (low) → **Black** (mid) → **Accelerator** (high). It's a deal-priority ladder: Accelerator gets deals placed for them, Black is 2nd in line, Premium is eligible. Know every tier cold.
## 🎯 How to sell the ladder
- **Sell HIGH (Accelerator) first.** We capitalize on buyers who can afford it — always lead there.
- **Downsell to Black ($997) only if, on the closing call, they genuinely can't afford Accelerator.** Never open with the cheaper option.
- **Premium ($49/mo)** is the entry tier + upsell engine: get them in cheap, then upsell on the free Monday/Wednesday calls.
---
## 🥉 Premium — $49/month *(low)*
- **Premium role** in the Discord.
- **Eligible for deals** — and your DMs actually get answered.
- **Loom walkthrough + SOP.**
**Fulfillment:** Premium Discord role + Loom + SOP.
**Checkout:** Fanbasis → "Thank You For Buying" page with a setup video (how to work it + join Discord) → upsell.
## 🥈 Black — $997 one-time *(mid)*
- **Black role — 2nd in line for deals.**
- **Everything in Premium.**
- **The course: "Scale to $10K"** (on Whop, #bootcamp).
**Fulfillment:** Black Discord role + everything in Premium + the course.
## 🥇 Accelerator — $4,000–$5,000 *(high)* [LOCK exact price]
*The flagship — sell this first.*
- **The full program:** brand deals **actively placed for you**, **priority support**, and **private channels.**
- Everything in Premium + Black, plus the group coaching cadence (1–2 calls/week on top of Friday).
### 🎯 The Closer's 3 HT Pillars (know these cold)
1. **Education** — the full course + knowledge channels.
2. **Coaching & Access** — priority support + group calls + private channels.
3. **Placement** — the team actively places you on brand deals *(worked, never guaranteed)* + the untimed **$5K/month** guarantee.
> 🚨 **COMPLIANCE — ALL TIERS, NON-NEGOTIABLE:** NEVER say "guaranteed brand deals" — not on calls, texts, or DMs. Even for Accelerator, it's "actively placed / worked to place," never promised. The ONLY guarantee is **$5K/month at some point (untimed)**. Keep "$6.5K/45 days" as *observed average — results vary.* (Hard legal line from Brady.)
> ⚙️ **Ops rules:** Keep the Discord CLEAN — the tier is a ROLE (Premium → Black → Accelerator), not a channel maze. The role is what unlocks deal access + priority. Course lives on **Whop** (#bootcamp), not Skool. Free **Mon/Wed calls** = the upsell engine; **Friday** = member group coaching.
> 📌 **Open items to lock (Daniel + Brady):** exact Accelerator price ($4K vs $5K) + payment plan? · does the untimed $5K guarantee apply to Accelerator only, or Black too? · exact private-channel / VIP-channel list (keep it lean).
> **Downstream to update (all still reference the old single $1,497):** closer pitch (Scripts Hub), setter financial-qualify, Kit sequences, PandaDoc agreements, Typeform budget buckets. Tracking forms + sheets are already synced to Premium / Black / Accelerator.

title: No-Close Process
body:
> 💡 A no-close is NOT a no-forever. Most closes happen on the 2nd or 3rd touch. Log everything. Stay in the game. The money is in the follow-up.
### Immediately After the Call
1. **Log detailed CRM notes** — What they said, where they hesitated, exact objections raised, their financial situation, what they said success looks like
2. **Update CRM status** to "No-Close — Follow Up"
3. **Notify setter via Slack** to begin follow-up sequence
4. **Set a follow-up task** for 24–48 hours out
---
### Follow-Up Sequence
**Within 24 Hours (Setter SMS):**
*"Hey [Name], [Closer] mentioned you two had a great call. Just following up — any questions after sitting on it?"*
**48–72 Hours (Closer outreach):**
*"Hey [Name] — I know the timing might not be perfect right now. I do have a spot that just opened up this week. Did you want to revisit the plan we built for you?"*
**Day 5 (Value drop):**
*Send a relevant case study: "Thought you'd find this useful — this is exactly what [similar person] did after being in your position."*
**Day 10 (Final close attempt):**
*"[Name], I want to be straight with you — I only have [X] spots left at this price point. After this, the next available slot is [timeframe]. If you want in, now is the time."*

title: Compensation & Pay Structure
body:
> 💰 This page covers exactly how you get paid, when, and what affects your check. Read it fully. If you have questions after reading this, ask management — don't assume.
---
## 📞 Setter Compensation
> 🟢 Rate: 5% commission on every deal that closes from a call you booked and showed.
>
> Example: You book a lead who closes a $5,000 deal — you earn $250.
- You get paid when the deal closes — not when you book the call
- If a lead no-shows or doesn't close, you do not earn on that booking
- If a client refunds within the refund window, your commission is clawed back
- Payment processed: weekly, every Friday, on deals verified in Close CRM
- Payment method: confirmed with you individually at onboarding (Stripe, PayPal, or bank transfer)
---
## 🎯 Closer Compensation
> 🟢 Rate: 10% commission on every deal you close, based on collected amount.
>
> Example: $5,000 deal = $500. $10,000 deal = $1,000.
- Commission is based on the collected amount — not the invoice amount
- Payment plans: you earn on each installment as it collects, not upfront on the full value
- If a client refunds within the refund window, your commission is clawed back
- Payment processed: weekly, every Friday, on cash collected and verified in Close CRM
- Payment method: confirmed with you individually at onboarding (Stripe, PayPal, or bank transfer)
---
## 📊 How Deals Get Tracked
- All closed deals are tracked in Close CRM — this is the source of truth
- Setter credit is assigned to the rep who booked the showing call (must be logged in CRM at time of booking)
- Closer credit is assigned to the rep logged as the opportunity owner in CRM at time of close
- Disputes must be raised within 48 hours of payment processing — contact Daniel directly by Slack DM
> ⚠️ If CRM is not updated, we cannot verify and you will not be paid. CRM hygiene is non-negotiable.
---
## 🔄 Refunds & Chargebacks
- Refund window: per the client agreement — confirm with Daniel before you ever quote refund terms on a call. Never improvise refund language.
- If a client refunds: both setter and closer commissions on that deal are clawed back on the next payment cycle
- If a chargeback is filed: commission is clawed back AND may result in a performance review
- High refund rates (3+ in a month) trigger a mandatory coaching call and performance review
---
## 🎁 Performance Bonuses
- Setter bonus: announced in Slack 1-general as monthly milestones go live (e.g., show-rate and booking-volume bonuses)
- Closer bonus: announced in Slack 1-general as monthly milestones go live (e.g., close-rate and cash-collected milestones)
- Bonuses are paid at end of month and are discretionary unless otherwise agreed in writing
---
## ⚖️ Pay Disputes
- If you believe your commission was calculated incorrectly, message Daniel within 48 hours of receiving your payment summary
- Include: deal name, close date, CRM link, and what you believe the discrepancy is
- Disputes raised after 48 hours will be reviewed but are not guaranteed to be resolved in your favor
> 🔇 Do NOT bring pay disputes into public Slack channels — DM management only.

title: Scripts Hub
body:
> 📝 Your scripts live here. These are the exact frameworks your setters and closers use on every call. Customize the specifics per client — the structure never changes.
---
## 📞 Setter Script — The Vault (Brady)
> 🎯 Objective: Triage the lead, qualify intent and finances, build curiosity, and book the call. You are not the closer — your job is to qualify and get them on the calendar.
### Step 1: Greeting + Curiosity
*"Hey [Name], this is [Setter] from Brady's team at The Vault. How did you find out about Brady?"*
- Warm, genuine tone. You are not reading — you are having a conversation.
### Step 2: Frame the Call
*"Quick call to make sure we are a fit before your appointment. I have just a few questions — shouldn't take more than 5–10 minutes. Sound good?"*
### Step 3: Basic Qualification
- "Where are you at with UGC right now — are you already doing deals, or just getting started?"
- "What are you making per month right now — from your job, UGC, everything?"
- "What are you trying to achieve in the next 3–6 months?"
- "How long have you been trying to figure this out?"
### Step 4: Financial Qualification
*"Just so I know we are on the same page — people who work with Brady typically invest somewhere around $1,000–$1,500 to get started. Is that a range you are able to work with?"*
- Indirect approach. Let them answer. Do not fill the silence.
### Step 5: Redirect
- If they pause on money: "I get it — it's a big decision. That's exactly why the call exists, so you can ask directly whether it makes sense for you."
- If they ask too many questions: "Great question — that's actually what the call is for. Our closer will walk you through everything, including exactly how placement works."
- If they ask "are brand deals guaranteed?": "Great question for the call — what I can tell you is the team actively places members, and the average member is around $6.5K/month after about 45 days. Nobody here will tell you deals are guaranteed — anyone who does is lying to you."
### Step 6: Filler + Rapport
- "What made you actually fill out the application? What was the thing that pushed you to do it?"
- "How long has making UGC your full income been on your mind?"
- "What have you tried before? Why didn't that work?"
### Step 7: Book the Call
*"Perfect — I'm going to book you in with [Closer] for [DATE/TIME]. You'll get a confirmation text and email. Show up 5 minutes early, have somewhere quiet, and come ready to take action. Sound good?"*
- Confirm name, phone, email, and time zone before hanging up.
- **Log detailed notes in Close CRM immediately after the call. Note quality = closer performance.**
---
## 🎯 Closer Script — The Vault (Brady)
> 🎯 Objective: Build genuine trust, create the perspective shift, present the offer with confidence, and close. Every phase has a purpose. Execute all five.
> 🚨 CRITICAL: The Perspective Shift (Phase 2) is the single most important step. Skipping it kills the close. No exceptions — always do it before pitching.
### Phase 1: Rapport Building (5–10 min)
- "Tell me a bit about yourself — what do you do right now?"
- "What has your experience with UGC been like so far?"
- "What made you book this call specifically?"
- Goal: get them talking. The more they talk, the more you learn. Listen for their real pain, not just their surface answer.
### Phase 2: Perspective Shift (2–3 min) — THE MOST CRITICAL STEP
*"[Name], I want to ask you something honest. You said you have been thinking about [GOAL] for [X months/years]. What do you think has been stopping you from getting there? … And if you keep doing exactly what you are doing now, where do you think you will be in 12 months? Same place? … So the question is not really whether you want this — you clearly do. The question is: are you going to do something different this time, or sit on it again? I am not judging — I just want to know who I am talking to."*
### Phase 3: Pitch Transition (1–2 min)
*"Okay. I appreciate you being real with me. So here is what we have been building — and I think it directly addresses what you have been missing. Let me walk you through it."*
### Phase 4: The Pitch (The Vault Accelerator)
- Walk the stack through THEIR pain: the 3-module course (mindset → content → business/negotiation), Friday group calls, 24/7 priority chat, content feedback from top-100 creators (Will & Dave approve your content before your first deal), and active brand deal placement through Sideshift while the team works its brand relationships.
- Expected timeline: realistic 45–90 days — first deal → $5K months → $10K+. Average member is ~$6.5K/month after about 45 days. $200K+ already paid out to creators.
- One relevant proof point tied to their specific situation (see Case Studies page).
- Investment: $1,497 one-time, lifetime access. Present confidently, do not apologize for the price. Anchor it against one decent brand deal paying it back.
- The guarantee: they make $5K/month at some point — no time bound. NEVER say "guaranteed brand deals."
- Urgency: real only — the space is early, brands are locking in creators now, CPM-only is what waiting looks like. No fake scarcity, ever.
### Phase 5: Post-Pitch + Final Commitment
- "So based on everything we talked about — does this make sense for where you're at?"
- "What questions do you have before we get you started?"
- Handle all objections using the Objection Handling Cheat Sheet in Closing Team SOPs
- **Final ask: "Alright [Name] — are you ready to get started?"**

## 📞 Setter SMS Templates
### Speed to Lead — Minute 1 (Send BEFORE calling)
*"Hey [Name]! Saw your application just came through for Brady's program — I'm reaching out now. Calling you in 2 minutes, keep an eye out!"*
### No Answer — Attempt 1
*"Hey [Name], this is [Your Name] from Brady's team — just tried calling about your application. When's a good time to connect real quick?"*
### No Answer — Attempt 2 (1 hour later)
*"Hey [Name], tried you again — no worries! Drop me a time that works and I'll call you then. Takes 5 minutes, just want to make sure you have everything you need."*
### No Answer — Attempt 3 (Same day, final)
*"Hey [Name], last try for today — I don't want your application to just sit here. If you're still interested in [OUTCOME], just reply and I'll make it work around your schedule."*
### Booking Confirmed (Send immediately after booking)
*"You're locked in, [Name]! 🔥 Your call with [CLOSER NAME] is set for [DATE] at [TIME]. Check your email for the calendar invite. Before the call, make sure you watch [PRE-CALL MATERIAL LINK] — it's required."*

### 2-Hour Reminder

### Day-Before Re-Confirmation (No reply to 2-hour reminder)

---
## 👻 No-Show Sequence
### No-Show — Minute 5
*"Hey [Name], we had you scheduled right now with [CLOSER NAME]. Everything okay? If something came up, no worries — just let me know and I'll get you rescheduled."*
### No-Show — Hour 1

*"Hey [Name], last follow-up from me. I know timing isn't always right, but if [OUTCOME] is still on your mind, Brady's team is here when you're ready. Here's the link to book: [BOOKING LINK]. No pressure."*
---
## 🔄 Re-Engagement Templates
### Cold Re-Engage — 2 to 4 Weeks

### Cold Re-Engage — 1+ Month
*"[Name], random but I was going through my pipeline and thought of you. A few people in similar situations to yours have had [RESULT] recently. Still something you're interested in? Happy to jump on a quick call."*

## 🎯 Closer SMS Templates
### Pre-Call Intro (Same day as booking)
*"Hey [Name], it's [CLOSER NAME] — I'll be on your call [DATE] at [TIME]. Just wanted to introduce myself early. Looking forward to it — this is my number if you need anything before then."*

### Post-Call — No-Close (Send within 30 min)
*"[Name], really enjoyed our conversation today. I know it's a big decision — take the time you need. I'm here if any questions come up. Don't sit on it too long though — spots genuinely do move."*
### No-Close Follow-Up — Day 2
*"Hey [Name], [CLOSER NAME] here. Just checking in — any questions after sitting on it? Sometimes things get clearer after a night. Happy to hop on a quick 10-min call if it helps."*

title: Slack Channels Guide
body:
> 💬 Workspace: [**thevaultugc.slack.com**](http://thevaultugc.slack.com) — your invite comes from Daniel by DM. Channels are numbered by importance. Channels are for signal; questions go to Daniel by DM.
### The Channels
- **1-general** — Team HQ. Announcements, pinned resources, anything team-wide. Everyone keeps this unmuted.
- **2-new-applications** — Every application (full AND partial) lands here automatically. This is the setter's starting gun: first contact within 5 minutes of the post. **Setters: set this channel to All Messages notifications — a muted setter is a dead funnel.** First setter to claim a lead in the channel owns it.
- **3-calls-booked** — Booking confirmations post here automatically.
- **4-no-show-police** — Every no-show posts here for recovery and rebooking. No-shows are the #1 funnel leak; this channel exists so none slip.
- **5-payment-success** — High-ticket payment confirmations. Celebrate loudly.
- **6-low-ticket-payments** — Low-ticket purchases, kept separate so the main payment channel stays signal. Mutable if you don't act on it.
- **7-eod-reminders** — The automated evening EOD reminder. Mutable if you already never miss.
- **8-eods** — Where you post your end-of-day numbers: Calls Made / Booked / Taken / Closed / Revenue / Notes. If you were off, post OFF and the reason. Pure data — no chatter.
### Rules
- Update the CRM before you post the win.
- If something's broken — a link, a zap, a calendar — say so in 1-general immediately.
- Pay questions: DM Daniel only, never in channels (see Compensation & Pay Structure).

title: Brady's Story
body:
> Know this story. On a closer call, you're not just selling a program — you're selling Brady. When a prospect hesitates, this story is what closes them.
### Who Is Brady?
Brady is a 22-year-old from the Chicago suburbs who went to Iowa. In high school he was a dead-broke Walmart stoner; in college he was the broke frat kid. Instead of waiting for a degree to pay off, he built **onebuzz**, a college media company that did roughly **$1M in revenue** and grew to about **1M followers**. Then he built [**Seatstock.com**](http://Seatstock.com) — a ticketing platform that reached about a **quarter-million users**, approached **8-figure revenue**, employed a **40-person team**, and raised **$600–700K — at 19 years old**.
When he found UGC, he made **$10K in his first month**. He realized the space was full of creators who could make content but had no idea how to run it like a business — so he started **The Vault** to teach creators how to land and scale brand deals through Sideshift, backed by real agency-side brand relationships.

title: Objection Handling Cheat Sheet
body:
> 🎯 **The one rule:** an objection is not a "no" — it's a request for more certainty. You never argue. Your job is to make the yes feel safe. Calm, curious, on their side. You're the big brother who's already been where they are, not a guru pushing them.
## The Method — run every objection through this
**Listen fully → Acknowledge → Isolate → Reframe → Confirm & close.**
1. **Listen fully.** Let them finish. Don't jump in. Silence after they speak makes them keep talking — and the *real* objection usually comes out second.
2. **Acknowledge.** "That's fair." "I get it." Never say "but." Lower the wall before you address anything.
3. **Isolate.** Find the REAL objection: *"If that weren't an issue, is this a yes?"* → If yes, solve that one thing. → If no, there's a deeper objection. Keep digging.
4. **Reframe.** Shift how they see it — with proof, logic, or a story. Change the frame; don't fight the fact.
5. **Confirm & close.** "Does that make sense?" → then move straight to the next step. Never leave an objection hanging in the air.
> 🧠 **Every objection is really one of three. Diagnose the root before you answer — most reps answer the wrong one:**
> ① **"Does this actually work?"** → they doubt the vehicle → answer with mechanism + proof.
> ② **"Will it work for ME?"** → they doubt themselves → answer with a case study of someone just like them + reassurance.
> ③ **"Do I trust you / this?"** → they've been burned before → answer with track record, honesty, and risk reversal.
> 🔥 **The Perspective Shift is your #1 move — do it BEFORE they object.** Put their goal in perspective, show them the gap between where they are and where they say they want to be, and get a commitment question answered ("if you keep doing exactly what you're doing, where are you in 12 months?"). Skip it and the close dies.
---
## 💬 General Objections
### "I need to think about it"
**Root:** hidden objection — nobody needs to "think about" something they're certain about.
**Response:** "Totally fair — what specifically do you want to think through? Let's talk it through right now. I'd rather answer it here than have you sitting on it alone."
Then isolate: "Is it more the money, the time, or whether this'll actually work for you?" Whatever they name is the real objection — go handle THAT one.
### "I don't have the money / I can't afford it"
**Root:** ② belief in the return, or priority — rarely literal.
**Response:** "I hear you. Quick question — if money wasn't the issue, would this be a yes?" → If yes, solve the money: "We do have a payment plan. And think about it this way — one placed brand deal can pay this back. Staying where you are costs you every month too."
> ⚠️ A payment plan EXISTS, but **never improvise the terms** — confirm exact numbers with Brady/Daniel before quoting anything. Always re-anchor to the outcome first; never drop price naked.
### "I'm not sure it'll work for me"
**Root:** ② self-belief.
**Response:** "That's fair — what would 'working' actually look like for you? … We had [similar member, same starting point] who had that exact worry — here's what happened." (Use a case study of someone LIKE them, not your biggest number.)
### "I need to talk to my spouse / partner"
**Root:** a real decision-maker, or a soft no. (They should've been qualified as the decision-maker on the setter call.)
**Response:** "Totally get it — is it the decision itself, or just the courtesy of looping them in? … Want to grab them for a quick 10 minutes right now so I can answer both your questions directly?" If genuinely unavailable: frame the cost of waiting and lock a firm follow-up with both of them on.
### "I've tried things before and it didn't work"
**Root:** ③ trust — they've been burned (this whole space runs on a trust recession).
**Response:** "I appreciate you being straight with me. What exactly did you try, and what was missing? … Here's the honest difference — most programs hand you information and leave you to figure out placement alone. The gap was never your effort. It was placement, feedback, and positioning — and that's the part we actually do *with* you."
### "How do I know this isn't a scam / that you're legit?"
**Root:** ③ trust.
**Response:** "Great question — you should ask it. Brady built two real companies before UGC, raised almost $700K for one at 19. We've put over $200K into our creators' pockets. And I'll tell you the same thing we tell everyone: anyone promising you guaranteed brand deals is lying to you. We don't. We help place you, and we show you the receipts."
### "Why does it cost that / it's too expensive"
**Root:** price = value not built yet.
**Response:** Re-anchor to the outcome BEFORE the number, every time: "Compared to what? One decent retainer covers this and then pays you every month after. The average member's around $6,500 a month, about 45 days in — results vary, but that's the frame. This isn't a cost, it's the fastest way to that." Never apologize for the price.
---
## 🎬 Vault / UGC-Specific Objections
### "So the brand deals are guaranteed?"
**Response:** "No — and be careful with anyone in this space who says they are. What IS real: our team actively places members through The Vault's brand relationships on Sideshift, Will and Dave approve your content before your first deal so you're not guessing, and the average member's around $6.5K a month after ~45 days. The one guarantee Brady stands behind: you get to $5K/month — no time limit on it."
> 🚨 **NEVER say "guaranteed brand deals" — not on calls, texts, or DMs.** Placement is helped and actively worked, never guaranteed. The ONLY guarantee is $5K/month (untimed). This is a hard legal line from Brady. Keep "$6.5K/45 days" framed as *observed average — results vary.*
### "I can learn UGC for free on YouTube"
**Response:** "You can — free content is how most of our members started. The honest difference: free content teaches you to make videos. It doesn't get your work approved by top-100 creators before you pitch, and it doesn't come with a team that has direct brand relationships placing you. Information was never the bottleneck — placement and positioning are."
### "UGC is just a side hustle / the income stops"
**Response:** "Biggest myth in the space. Good content compounds — brands keep paying for what keeps performing, that's what a retainer is. The creator economy right now is rich-get-richer: treat it like a business and you get retainers with view minimums; treat it like a side hustle and you stack $50 CPM deals forever. Which one have you been doing?"
### "I've been doing UGC and can't land high-paying deals"
**Response:** "Then you're exactly who this was built for. You don't have a content problem — you have a positioning and business problem. That's module 3 plus the placement side: pricing yourself up, charging for usage rights, and having our team put you in front of brands instead of cold-applying with everyone else."
### "I need experience first / I'm brand new"
**Root:** ② self-belief / impostor.
**Response:** "Brands don't check a résumé. Most of the time your video runs on THEIR page, not yours — they're buying one thing: can you make a video that gets people to buy. That's learnable from video one, and the creators getting signed right now walked in with the same zero deals you have."
### "UGC is oversaturated / I'm too late"
**Root:** ① scarcity fear.
**Response:** "It's saturated at the bottom — a million creators fighting over $50 CPM deals. The top, where brands pay retainers to people they trust, is starving. The space is early. 'Too late' is only true if you plan on staying at the bottom."
### "I don't have time for this"
**Response:** "It's a couple hours a day from your phone — probably the same amount you're already scrolling. The real question isn't whether you have time. It's whether another 12 months in the same spot is worth not making it."
---
## 📞 Before the Call — Getting Them On It (dialing + no-shows)
Most "objections" never happen because the lead never picks up. Win here first.
> ⚡ **Speed-to-lead = 5 minutes, non-negotiable.** The moment an application hits (🌶️ Hot Leads / New App smart view in Close), you call. Intent falls off a cliff after the first few minutes.
- **Double-dial.** No answer? Hang up and call right back immediately. A second ring back-to-back reads as "this is important" and gets picked up far more often — then text.
- **The cadence** (run it off the Close smart view, log every touch): call → double-dial → text → wait → call → text, spacing out across the day, then daily. Don't quit after one try; don't hound forever — work the smart view until they book, DQ, or NGMI.
- **"I'm busy / can't talk":** "No problem — 90 seconds to see if it's even worth booking you a real call. Fair?" Or lock a firm time and send the calendar invite while you're still on the phone.
- **No-show:** call at the exact scheduled time (double-dial), text "we're live — jumping on?", then run the **No-Show Process**. Rebook once, keep it in the pipeline, work it via the smart view.
> 🔗 Deeper mechanics live in **Close CRM SOPs**, **No-Show Process**, and **Pre Call Sales Process** (this teamspace). This page = what to SAY. Those = how to run the CRM.

title: UGC Terminology
body:
Know these terms cold. When a prospect uses niche language, you match it. Matching their language builds instant credibility and trust — it signals that you understand their world.
---
### Core UGC Terms
- **UGC (User-Generated Content)** — Content creators make FOR brands to use in the brand's own marketing. The creator gets paid for the content itself; it usually runs on the brand's channels, not the creator's.
- **Brand Deal** — A paid agreement between a creator and a brand for content. The core unit of income in this space.
- **Sideshift** — The platform the UGC space runs on — it's where creators apply to deals and where payouts get processed. ~1M creators are on it. Vault members apply on Sideshift daily while the team places them.
- **CPM (Cost Per Mille)** — Payment per 1,000 views. Brands are moving newer creators onto **CPM-only deals** (you only earn based on views). Fine to start, a trap to stay in.
- **Retainer** — Fixed monthly payment from a brand for ongoing content — often with **view minimums** attached. This is how big brands pay established creators, and where members want to end up.
- **View Minimums** — A guaranteed floor of views a creator must hit for the brand to keep paying the retainer.
- **Rate Card** — A creator's price list per deliverable. Most creators price too low — "good services get paid higher premiums."
- **Deliverables** — Exactly what the creator owes the brand: number of videos, formats, revisions, deadlines.
- **Usage Rights** — How long and where the brand may run the creator's content. Longer usage = higher price. Creators who don't know this get robbed.
- **Whitelisting** — The brand runs ads from the creator's own account/handle. Priced separately from the content itself.
- **Hook** — The first 1–3 seconds of a video that stops the scroll. The single biggest factor in whether content performs.
- **Ad Creative** — Content made specifically to run as a paid ad. Brands buy winning UGC as ad creative — this is the higher-paying work.
---
### Vault-Specific Terms (our program language)
- **The Vault / The Accelerator** — Brady's program: course + community + placement. Members hold the **ACCELERATOR** role in Discord.
- **Whop** — The platform members buy through and access the bootcamp on. (Brady is connected with the Whop co-founders.)
- **The Bootcamp** — The structured onboarding content members request access to on Whop after joining.
- **Brand Deal Board** — The Discord board where deal opportunities are posted for members.
- **Will & Dave** — The Vault's content team. They review and approve every member's content before their first deal — this is the quality gate.
- **Friday Calls** — The weekly private group coaching calls.
---
> 💬 How this shows up on a call: a stuck creator says "I'm only getting CPM offers on Sideshift." You say: "Right — because brands put newer creators on CPM-only now. Retainers with view minimums are where the real money is, and that's a positioning problem, not a luck problem. That's literally what module 3 and the placement side fix."

title: No-Show Process
body:
> ⚠️ A no-show is not a lost deal. Most no-shows rebook if you follow the sequence correctly. Do NOT ghost them or mark them as lost without at least 3 follow-up touches.
### No-Show Sequence
**Minute 0:** Attempt call twice. Wait on the line for 2 minutes.
**Minute 5:** Send text — "Hey [Name], we had a call scheduled for [time]. Missed you — everything okay?"
**Hour 1:** Setter follows up via SMS with a softer check-in.
**Hour 24:** Setter makes 2nd attempt — "Hey [Name], I know life gets busy. Still interested in [goal]? We have [X] spots left this week."
**Day 3:** Send value (relevant case study or testimonial) + soft CTA. "Thought you'd find this useful — [case study]. Still happy to hop on a call if the timing works."
**Day 5+:** Move to long-term nurture in CRM if no response. Tag as "No-Show — Nurture".
---
### CRM Actions After No-Show
1. Update status to "No-Show" immediately
2. Log date/time of no-show in notes
3. Set a follow-up task for 24 hours out
4. Notify setter via Slack to begin follow-up sequence

title: Sales Calls Recordings
body:

title: Pre Call Sales Process
body:
> 🎯 Your pre-call process has one job: increase your show rate and increase your close rate. A 10-minute call before the main event can make or break the deal.
### How It Works
Every booked call gets a setter triage call immediately after booking. The setter qualifies further, gauges intent, confirms finances, gets verbal commitment to show, and sends pre-call assets (VSL, case studies).
Your job as the closer: Call the lead within minutes of booking to introduce yourself, surface hidden objections, and build anticipation for the gameplan call.
### 3 Objectives of Your Pre-Call
1. **Increase close rate** by introducing yourself and building rapport before the main call
2. **Increase show rate** with a second confirmation touchpoint and building curiosity around their gameplan
3. **Handle hidden objections** before they derail the main close call
---
### Pre-Call Script
**Opener:**
*"Hey [Name], it's [Closer] from Brady's team at The Vault — I see we have a call booked for [date]. Just calling to quickly introduce myself and see if you have any questions before we hop on."*
**If they haven't watched pre-call material:**
*"No problem — I'll shoot that over via text right now. Go through it before our call, it's required so you understand what we stand for. Sound good?"*
**Closing the pre-call:**
*"Perfect — I'll see you on the call. Looking forward to it. I'll text you my direct number so you can reach me if anything comes up before then."*
---
### Morning-Of: Voice Note
Send a voice note the morning of the call:
*"Hey [Name], super excited for our call today. Based on what I know about your situation, I've already built out a gameplan I think you're going to like. Just shoot me a text confirming you're still good for [time]."*
**If no reply within 2 hours:**
*"Hey [Name], all good for our call today — just drop me a thumbs up so I know we're on."*
> ❌ If the prospect hasn't responded to any confirmation (setter, you, or the dialer) within 24 hours — the call is cancelled from your calendar. Do not hold time for ghosts.

title: Fundamental Checklist / Qualifications
body:
> ✅ This is the gate. If a lead doesn't pass, they don't get booked. When in doubt, don't book — a bad booking costs the closer a slot and costs you credibility.
### The 5 Fundamentals (ALL must be true to book)
1. **Moderate-to-high intent** — they can articulate why they're reaching out NOW, not "just curious"
2. **Warmed up to Brady** — they've consumed his content and know who he is
3. **Genuine desire for change** — a real pain point; staying where they are is not acceptable to them
4. **Access to funds** — minimum $1–2K liquid, ideally more. Good Vault leads are already making $1–5K/month. Dead broke = DQ, full stop.
5. **Decision-maker confirmed** — spouse/partner situation surfaced on the triage call, not discovered on the close call
### Vault-Specific Non-Negotiables
- **Not afraid of the camera** — nervous is coachable, unwilling is a DQ
- **Hungry and ready to work** — the average member hits ~$6.5K/month after 45 days because they DO the work
- **Realistic on timeline** — they accept 45–90 days to first real results. Anyone demanding day-one money is a future refund.
### Booking Overrides
Exceptions to the checklist exist, but you need a good reason — and the reason gets logged in the CRM notes so the closer sees it walking in. "Felt good energy" is not a reason.
### Quick DQ Reference
Tire-kicker · dead broke with no path to funds · can't decide without 3 approvals · negative/confrontational on triage · zero content consumption · goal doesn't match the program · lazy/scared/uncommitted · overthinker who won't act

title: Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) Cheatsheet
body:
> ✅ This is the filter. If a lead doesn't pass this checklist, they don't get booked. There are exceptions — but you need a good reason to override this. When in doubt, don't book.
### Fundamental Qualification Checklist (ALL must be true to book)
1. **Has moderate to high intent** — They WANT this, not just curious. Can they articulate why they're reaching out now?
2. **Warmed up to Brady** — Has consumed his content. Knows who he is. Not coming in completely cold.
3. **Has genuine desire for change** — Identifiable pain point. They have a reason to buy. Status quo is not acceptable to them.
4. **Has access to funds** — Minimum $1K–2K liquid. Ideally $5K+. If they literally have nothing, this isn't the right time.
5. **Is the decision-maker** — Spouse/partner situation is confirmed. No "I need to ask my wife" surprise on the close call.
---
### ICP Profile — Who We're Looking For
**Age Range: **18–30, mostly male, middle to upper-middle class — "internet money" kids with actual personality, not just money-obsessed. Hustle over academics.
**Situation: **Making ~$1–5K/month — a job or corporate role they want out of, or a stuck UGC creator who can't crack high-paying deals, or brand-new and hungry. NOT dead broke — they have money to invest.
**Biggest Pain: **Can't land high-paying brand deals. Can't go viral. Don't know where to start. Camera fear, mindset, time management. Watching other creators get rich while they stack cheap deals.
**Dream Outcome: **$10–20K months. Quit the job. The car. 2–3 hour workdays. Freedom and the finer things — with reassurance that the risk is safe to take.
**What They've Already Tried: **Grinding UGC solo on cheap CPM deals, posting without strategy, other UGC courses/gurus that were all info and no placement.
**Realistic Timeline (set this expectation): **45–90 days. Milestones: first deal → $5K months → $10K+.
**Limiting Beliefs to Break on Calls: **"It's just a side hustle" / "content doesn't pay day one" / "the income stops." Truth: good content compounds — it gets paid month after month.
**Non-Negotiables: **Not afraid of the camera. Hungry. Ready to work.
---
### Red Flags — Do NOT Book These People
- **Tire-kickers** — "Just checking it out" / no urgency / no clear reason to change now
- **No money, no path to money** — Truly zero capital and no financing options. Don't waste the closer's time.
- **Can't make a decision** — Needs 3 people's approval before doing anything. Spouse is a blocker and they haven't handled it.
- **Negative/confrontational attitude** — Dismissive, rude, or cynical on the triage call. These people are a nightmare to close and onboard.
- **Zero content consumption** — Never seen a single video. Doesn't know [CLIENT NAME]. Complete cold lead with no warmth.
- **Clearly wrong fit for the offer** — Their goal doesn't match what the program delivers. Don't force a square peg.
- **Lazy, scared, or uncommitted** — Brady's bad-fit list. Overthinkers who need certainty before action don't survive the first 45 days.
- **Terrified of the camera with no willingness to fix it** — camera comfort is a non-negotiable for UGC. Nervous is fine; unwilling is a DQ.
